active is a visibility gate invalidated in execute finally; escaped/late Session calls must reject before JDBC use. Volatile does not make the connection cross-thread safe: guard also binds the original callback thread.

backupCommitted publishes only the committed begin state; guarded operations require matching immutable backupBegins and original run. Visibility is not a surrogate for durable SQL/readback or native ownership.

handoffStarted is the one-attempt publication flag for callback-scoped maintenance handoff. Original-thread guard still forbids concurrent use; it is not a retry lease or permission to repeat an unconfirmed operation.

inHandoff gates parent operations while its advisory lock is intentionally borrowed by a synchronous child. Guarded lifetime/thread checks remain necessary; volatile is visibility, not proof of actual lock acquisition or child termination.
backupFinished gates post-terminal readback; matching committed handles and same callback are checked independently. A visible flag alone cannot mint genuine Backup or Root completion.

cleanupVerified gates later parent operations only after the existing seven-step verification returns. The connection and run are not exported; real row/Unit evidence is separate from this source applicability decision.

expiryHandoffStarted preserves the one-attempt state across guarded entry checks. It is not an atomic multi-step protocol or cross-thread JDBC permission; original-thread/lifetime/run/receipt predicates remain required.
